subject: Difference between pairwise comparison and disparity

messages.author: 38776402820404c2
messages.subject: Difference between pairwise comparison and disparity
parts:
Hi all,

I'm fairly new to geomorph and I'm trying to wrap my head around the significance of my data. I'll try to sketch the situation:

I have 182 samples of landmarked data (22 landmarks each), of which 13 species are 'outgroups' (ingroup is therefore 169). I made morphospaces of both datasets (ingroup separately, and ingroup + outgroup combined), and labelled the points based on the species' host-association. I want to know if the mean shapes of these points clouds (convex hulls) are significant different from one-another. Therefore I did a pairwise Procrustes ANOVA using the following script:

Procrustes <- gpagen(mydata, curves = slider_matrix)
y<-two.d.array(Procrustes$coords)
x<-as.factor(df$V4) #df is the dataframe, V4 is the host-association
Procrustes_anova <- procD.lm(y~x)
summary(Procrustes_anova)
PW <- pairwise(Procrustes_anova, groups = x, covariate = NULL)
summary(PW, show.vectors = TRUE, test.type = "dist")

In the morphospace with only the ingroup included, almost all groups were found to be siginificantly different (P <0.05), although the point clouds are all overlapping and barely any visual differences in the mean shapes were seen when performing plotRefToTarget. 
In the morphospace including the outgroups, which are outside of the overlapping point cloud, the P-values go up. Even in the comparison of clouds which (almost; due to new Procrustes superimpositioning) stay the same, the p-values change a lot. 

So my question here is: 
  • Am I doing this correct, and is the pairwise test using relative distances in the entire morphospace to seek for significance?
  • And when searching for an answer I found a lot of users use a disparity test to find between-group differences. How is this different from my current analysis? If I use morphol.disparity(Procrustes$coords ~ 1, groups = x), I get insiginificant values for all groups except for the outgroup - is disparity here a proxy for overlapping in the morphospace?
Thanks in advance, really appreciate it!

Best wishes, and groetjes from the Netherlands,
Werner de Gier

messages.author: f16866fc42d43e64
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Difference between pairwise comparison and disparity
parts:
Werner,

several points here:

1. Yes, your general approach for testing for group differences is correct
2. Keep in mind that p-values using a procD.lm anova is based on permutation of residuals (for more on this please see the RRPP package and corresponding papers). This means that if you change your sample (ingroup vs. ingroup+ougroup) the available data for running permutations change and as such p-values are also bound to change.
3. I am guessing that when looking at "overlap" of groups you are doing so in a PCA space. Keep in mind that this is a reduction of the total shape space on which ANOVA and pairwise comparisons are being run. As such, what you see "by eye" does not necessarily fully express the ANOVA tests. A PCA seeks general variation in your sample, which does not need to align with differentiation between groups (which is what ANOVA is looking at). Trust stats first, and then use a PCA to illustrate and explore patterns, would be my suggestion.
4. Kind of the same goes for deformation grids. If you KNOW (from your stats) that there are significant differences between your groups, and want to visualize those, go ahead and exaggerate shape differences using the mag argument in plotRefToTarget. Remember to say that you did so in the legend of your paper figure. If no significant differences exist, deformation grids are just a mathematical construct and not informative.
5. ANOVAs test for differences in mean shape among groups (and pairwise comparisons investigate which groups differ). As is the case for any ANOVA, this is done taking group dispersion into account (are differences between groups large enough in comparison to variation within groups?). Disparity analysis does a whole different thing, i.e. it tests for differences in the multivariate dispersion of your groups NOT their mean shapes. Depending on your biological question this can be informative, e.g. as to sources of morphological variation etc. I recommend you carefully read the help page of that function and corresponding cited papers for that, as it is an entire investigation field within morphometrics.

Hope this helps
Antigoni
